requested_scope: Full audit and remediation of all errors in code and in the customer workflow.
scope: Regulatory deadline correctness across API, engine and public copy
Server billing, entitlement reconciliation, checkout and tenant boundaries
Customer workflow: calculator entry save, checkout handoff and retry, upload intake
Accessibility of the authenticated application shell

fixed.issue: POST /api/checkout/verify used the wall clock as its ordering watermark, so the guard in syncSubscriptionRecord — which only accepts a write newer than the stored subscription_event_at — could never reject a replayed session. Revisiting an older confirmation link overwrote the customer's live subscription with the old, canceled one and still answered verified:true.
fixed.impact: Buy Growth, cancel, buy Pro, then open the old confirmation link: a paying Pro customer is 402'd off the plan they pay for, with recovery deferred to the next genuine Stripe event (up to a billing cycle). The client makes it reachable without deliberate abuse, because success_url always carries session_id and App auto-fires verify on any /app load with that param.
fixed.change: Watermark the sync with session.created (the purchase's own ordering key), falling back to the wall clock only when absent. A stale session is now skipped by the same guard that stops out-of-order webhooks and is reported as ok:true/stale_event, so the response still carries the correct current billing state.
fixed.tests: tests/audit-20261005-server.test.ts pins the watermark decision and that the cross-account ownership check is unchanged.

fixed.issue: The compliance dates lived in three disagreeing copies: /api/compliance/deadlines said SB 253 was due 2026-01-01, getComplianceStatus hardcoded a '2026-01-01 Scope 1 and Scope 2 reporting' next_deadline, and the public methodology page said August 10, 2026.
fixed.impact: On 2026-10-05 the API reported the SB 253 first-year deadline as overdue by roughly nine months while it was in fact about five weeks away. In a product sold on compliance, telling a customer they are late when they are not is a trust-destroying error.
fixed.change: Added compliance-deadlines.cjs as the single source of truth. SB 253 Scope 1/2 is 2026-11-10 (CARB deferred it from August 10 in the proposed Modified Regulations) carried explicitly as date_status 'proposed', because the deferral still depends on the comment period and OAL approval. Status and days_left derive from the current date; getComplianceStatus returns no deadline at all for a framework that does not apply; the public copy states the deferral and tells readers to confirm with CARB.
fixed.tests: tests/compliance-deadlines.test.ts — 7 cases including the live regression window, past-date detection across four 2026 dates, UTC day-boundary behaviour, and non-applicable frameworks.

fixed.issue: getComplianceStatus carried the deadline text as a static string with no date awareness, and /api/compliance/deadlines returned the same static entries to every company with no applicability signal.
fixed.change: Both read the shared table. The endpoint now returns days_left, a date_status and an explicit applicability:'unknown' with a note, rather than implying every framework applies to every tenant.

fixed.issue: Two defects in one function, both about CSRD. (a) Stale date: the deadline table carried csrd_wave2 due_date 2026-12-31, 'wave 2 companies report for FY2025'. Directive (EU) 2025/794 ('Stop-the-Clock', OJ L 2025/794 of 16.4.2025, in force 17 April 2025) postponed wave 2 by two years, so it is 2028 for FY2027. (b) Contradictory threshold: getComplianceStatus hardcoded `region in EU && employees >= 500`, while the same table's wave 2 row said 'EU entities with 250+ employees'.
fixed.impact: Latent, not live. /api/companies/:id/compliance already answers 501 for real tenants because company revenue/employees/region are not modelled, and both sample companies are region CA, so nothing customer-facing changes today. When an EU tenant is supported, (a) would tell wave 2 customers they owe a sustainability statement on a date that stopped being legally correct around eighteen months earlier, and (b) would report every EU company with 251-500 employees as not_applicable with a null deadline, contradicting the product's own table. Same failure shape as COMP-01: a hardcoded date outliving the regulation, plus a second reader of the table disagreeing with the first.
fixed.change: Wave 2 moved to due_date 2028-12-31 with previously_scheduled '2026-12-31' retained for audit and the Directive cited in the file header; wave 1 deliberately left on its unmodified 2025 date because the postponement did not touch it. Applicability no longer restated in code: every deadline row now carries a machine-readable `applies` block (regions / min_revenue / min_employees) alongside its human `applies_to` string, with deadlineAppliesTo() and deadlinesApplicableTo() as the single reader. getComplianceStatus selects from those rows instead of computing thresholds. `applicable` is now derived from whether ANY deadline for the framework applies, so scope no longer flips to 'not applicable' merely because the date passed; `in_scope_deadlines` exposes what the company is actually on the hook for.
fixed.sources: Directive (EU) 2025/794, verified against the primary text on EUR-Lex on 2026-10-05: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2025/794/oj/eng — wave 2 'to report in 2026 for financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2025', and 'the sustainability reporting requirements for those undertakings should be postponed by two years'. Transposition deadline 31 December 2025.
fixed.tests: tests/compliance-deadlines.test.ts COMP-03 block — 9 cases: the superseded date is gone and the previous one is retained, wave 1 is unchanged, a 251-employee EU company is in scope with a 2028 deadline, a 250-employee one is not, applicability agrees with the table at seven headcount boundaries including both sides of each threshold, SB 253 scope 1/2 still precedes scope 3, scope survives every deadline passing, and region matching is checked against the real shipped row (both 'EU' and 'europe' spellings, plus the state fallback).

fixed.issue: A successful emission-entry INSERT followed by a failed list re-read was reported as 'Failed to add emission entry'. The form keeps its values on a thrown error, so pressing 'Add Entry' again wrote a second row for the same activity.
fixed.impact: Silently inflated the dashboard totals, the report aggregates and the PDF for an audit artifact, with no warning.
fixed.change: A refresh failure is now caught separately and surfaced as its own notice that warns against re-adding; the form clears because the write genuinely succeeded. Insert failures are re-thrown as real Errors so the customer sees the actual reason (RLS denial, quota, constraint) instead of a generic string.
fixed.tests: tests/emission-entry-save.test.ts drives the real form — including that a refresh-only failure still clears the form and warns, and that a genuine insert failure retains the values.

fixed.issue: stripe.checkout.sessions.create had no idempotency key, so two concurrent /api/checkout calls (double-click, or a retry after a network timeout) both passed the check-then-act 'no active subscription' guard and both created a live billable session.
fixed.change: Added a deterministic user+price+window idempotency key so a retry returns the same session.

fixed.issue: reports.period is an unconstrained TEXT column and the report-generate route validated nothing, unlike the summary route, so any authenticated account could persist a ~100 KB string per request under the global rate limit.
fixed.change: Shares SUMMARY_PERIOD_PATTERN and rejects before the insert.

fixed.issue: /app was the only customer-facing route shell without id='main-content', so the route-change focus move was a silent no-op and keyboard/screen-reader users had no named main landmark on any paid page.
fixed.change: The authenticated shell now defines the same focus target the other eight route shells use.

fixed.issue: A failed checkout erased its intent from the URL before the POST resolved and offered no retry, so a reload or any later navigation discarded a purchase the customer had already chosen.
fixed.change: The intent is stripped only on success (where the browser leaves for Stripe); failure keeps it and the error banner now offers a working 'Retry checkout' button that rebuilds the identical request.

fixed.issue: The destructive delete named the raw catalog key ('natural_gas') while the row read 'Natural gas', so the customer could not verify which irreversible action they were approving.
fixed.change: Confirm text and the button's accessible name both use the row label.

fixed.issue: DataIntake had no re-entry guard on the hidden file input, so overlapping upload loops raced and the slower one overwrote the newer results; results were also keyed by file name alone, colliding across folders.
fixed.change: Guarded re-entry, disabled the input during upload, and keyed outcomes by name plus position.

fixed.issue: ReportGenerator.tsx called URL.revokeObjectURL synchronously immediately after link.click(). Releasing the object URL in the same turn as the click frees the blob before the browser has read it.
fixed.impact: Chrome tolerates this; Firefox and Safari resolve the download asynchronously and the click produces no file at all. Line 58 then unconditionally set 'Report generated and downloaded.' — so on those browsers the product's headline paid action reported success while delivering nothing, with no error state and no retry. In a product whose output is the customer's audit artifact, a silently missing PDF is worse than a visible failure.
fixed.change: The download now goes through one shared helper, src/lib/api.ts downloadBlob(), which defers the revoke with window.setTimeout(..., 10_000) past the point where the download turn has resolved, so the object URL is still freed rather than leaked.
fixed.tests: tests/customer-journey-regressions.test.tsx CJU-01 — stubs URL.createObjectURL/revokeObjectURL and anchor click, then asserts the revoke has NOT fired once the handler settles, and separately that advancing past the delay DOES fire it so deferring cannot silently become leaking. Verified non-vacuous by reverting the fix: both cases fail against the old synchronous revoke.

fixed.issue: The same revoke-before-download defect existed a second time, independently, in Settings.tsx handleExportData — the GDPR self-serve data export. Two copies of the same anchor-and-revoke dance, both wrong in the same way.
fixed.impact: Materially worse than CJU-01 because this is a statutory right: a customer exercising their GDPR Article 15 data-access right clicked 'Export my data', and on Firefox or Safari no file was produced, while the banner immediately confirmed 'Your data export has been downloaded as a machine-readable JSON file.' A customer who cannot obtain their own data cannot exercise their rights, and the confirmation actively misleads them.
fixed.change: Rather than fix the second copy independently, both now call one shared downloadBlob() in src/lib/api.ts, so a third blob download cannot reintroduce it. A guard test asserts neither caller contains createObjectURL or revokeObjectURL again. Settings' data-notice, data-error, billing-error and billing-loading regions also gained role=status / role=alert, matching the convention already used in DataIntake and the calculator.
fixed.tests: tests/customer-journey-regressions.test.tsx SET-01 — three cases covering the helper's timing behaviour directly, plus regression guards that both callers use it and neither has re-introduced the raw dance.

fixed.issue: AuthCallback read `searchParams.get('error')` to detect an OAuth failure, but the InsForge SDK deletes that param before React Router ever sees it. Its Auth constructor calls detectAuthCallback(), which runs cleanUrlParams('error') before its first await — synchronously, at createClient() evaluation during module import, and src/App.tsx statically imports src/lib/insforge, so the strip always wins the race.
fixed.impact: Two failures. First, the branch was dead code: a visitor who denied consent or hit an IdP fault got the generic 'We could not finish signing you in' instead of the reason, even though error_description — which the SDK does NOT strip — was sitting in the URL being ignored. Second and worse, with `error` gone the effect fell through to getCurrentUser(), which in browser mode answers from any session in local storage. So a failed OAuth round trip on a browser holding a stale session navigated to /app as if sign-in had succeeded, and the user was never told anything had failed.
fixed.change: error_description is now read in its own right and drives the short-circuit alongside error, so the effect cannot reach getCurrentUser() on a failed callback. The rendered message prefers the provider's description. `error` is still read, so the code is correct if a future SDK stops stripping it.
fixed.tests: tests/auth-flow-regressions.test.ts — a source guard asserts the short-circuit keys off error_description as well as error, and that the provider-error early-return precedes the navigation. Verified non-vacuous by reverting the short-circuit: the guard fails.

fixed.issue: The OAuth-failure recovery link on AuthCallback was a bare <Link to="/login">, and that path never called takeAuthIntent(). The retry then actively destroyed the intent: startProviderSignIn calls saveAuthIntent(intent ?? null), and with no intent on the URL that removes the sessionStorage key.
fixed.impact: A prospect who picked Growth/annual, failed one Google attempt, and retried from this link landed on a bare /app after signing in — the selected plan and the checkout were silently dropped. A lost sale presented to the customer as a successful login.
fixed.change: Added peekAuthIntent(), a non-destructive read, because takeAuthIntent() consumes by design so a completed purchase cannot be replayed and cannot be used by a screen that only wants to forward the intent. The recovery link now carries ?plan=&billing= so the retry resumes the checkout.
fixed.tests: tests/auth-flow-regressions.test.ts — asserts peekAuthIntent() is idempotent across repeated reads while takeAuthIntent() still consumes exactly once, that a corrupted or unknown stored intent reads as null, and that AuthCallback's retry link carries the plan.

fixed.issue: Signup never read `?redirect=`, while Login forwarded it. App.tsx sends anonymous visitors on a protected route to /login?redirect=<path+search> (and does the same on mid-session expiry), and Login copies all search params onto /signup — where destinationFor(intent) ignored them entirely.
fixed.impact: An anonymous visitor deep-linked to a protected route who chose 'Sign up' instead of 'Sign in' was dumped on /app after signup and again after email verification, never reaching the page they were trying to open.
fixed.change: Extracted Login's same-origin redirect validation into safeRedirectPath() in src/lib/authIntent.ts and routed Signup through it, so there is one reader for the open-redirect rule rather than two that can drift. Login's behaviour is unchanged.
fixed.tests: tests/auth-flow-regressions.test.ts — safeRedirectPath is exercised directly against the real bypass shapes (protocol-relative //host, backslash /\host, cross-origin absolute) and the same-origin pass-through; Signup is guarded to resolve through the helper and to carry no second copy of the validation.

fixed.issue: ForgotPassword's 'I already have a code' button set the reset step without setting `email`, but the step's subtitle interpolated `email`, which initialises to ''.
fixed.impact: Rendered literally 'If an account exists for , we've emailed a reset code.' — on exactly the path the button exists to serve, since that path is for users arriving in a new tab already holding a code.
fixed.tests: tests/auth-flow-regressions.test.ts guards that the interpolation is behind an email.trim() check and that the old unguarded template is gone.

fixed.issue: The 'Use a different email, or send another code' handler cleared the code but left password and confirm in component state.
fixed.impact: After a failed reset the previous new password survived the step swap, so re-requesting a code and stepping forward again showed a stale password that belonged to a code the customer no longer held — inviting a second failed attempt.
fixed.change: The handler now clears password and confirm as well as the code.
fixed.tests: tests/auth-flow-regressions.test.ts asserts the reset-step handler clears all three fields.

fixed.issue: The delete path carried two copies of the bug DATA-01 had already fixed on the insert path. handleDelete threw the InsForge SDK's plain error object, so EmissionList's `err instanceof Error` was false and every failure collapsed to 'Failed to delete entry', never the real reason. And because the post-delete re-read was unisolated, a refresh failure was reported as a failed delete.
fixed.impact: The real cause (an RLS denial, a constraint, a quota) was never shown to the customer. Worse, when the DELETE succeeded but the re-read failed, the row stayed on screen beside an error saying the delete failed — and every retry re-issued a DELETE for a row that no longer existed, so the UI could not be recovered without a manual reload.
fixed.change: handleDelete now throws a real Error carrying the server's message, mirroring the insert path, and wraps the re-read so a refresh failure sets the existing refreshNotice ('Entry deleted, but the list could not be refreshed...') instead of a delete error. EmissionList additionally reads .message off a non-Error throw and the banner carries role="alert" so a delete that fails while focus is elsewhere is announced rather than leaving the row looking untouched.
fixed.tests: tests/customer-journey-regressions.test.tsx CJU-02 — three cases driving the real component: the server's message is shown rather than the generic string, the banner is a role=alert live region, and a successful delete followed by a failing re-read produces the refresh notice and NO delete error.

fixed.issue: Dashboard.tsx treated any 400 or 403 — from either of two parallel requests — as 'no company yet'. The catch could not tell which request had failed, and a 403 is not a no-company signal.
fixed.impact: If the summary succeeded but the trend call returned 400/403, setEmissions was never reached and the render fell into the needsOnboarding branch: 'Welcome to EcoAuditor — your account is ready' for an existing account with real data. That screen has two navigation links and no retry, so the customer is stuck there with no way to recover except navigating away.
fixed.change: The fetch effect records which request failed. Only a 400 from the summary request is treated as onboarding; a trend failure or any 403 now falls through to the error branch, which carries a retry affordance.
fixed.tests: tests/customer-journey-regressions.test.tsx CJU-03 renders the real Dashboard against a stubbed fetch: a summary 400 does show onboarding, a trend 403 does not, a summary 403 does not, and the trend failure path offers a retry control.

fixed.issue: ReportGenerator styled its status with `status.startsWith('Error') ? 'text-risk-high' : 'text-risk-low'`, encoding severity as a message prefix. The plan gate sets 'Reports require an active plan — visit Pricing to upgrade.', which does not start with 'Error'.
fixed.impact: A blocked, non-upgraded action rendered in the same green (#16a34a) as a completed report download.
fixed.change: Status is now a {tone, message} object with tones error/warn/ok mapped through TONE_CLASS. The plan gate is 'warn' (amber, risk.medium), which is a real token in tailwind.config.js rather than an arbitrary colour.
fixed.tests: tests/customer-journey-regressions.test.tsx CJU-04 drives a real 402 upgrade_required response and asserts the rendered class is text-risk-medium and NOT text-risk-low.

fixed.issue: Three async result regions had no live region: the EmissionList delete-error banner, the ReportGenerator status line, and the Dashboard loading spinner text.
fixed.impact: A failed delete, a failed or successful report generation, and the dashboard content swapping in after its fetch were all silent for screen-reader users. The codebase already set role="alert"/role="status" correctly elsewhere (DataIntake.tsx, carbon-calculator/index.tsx), so this was an inconsistency rather than a missing convention.
fixed.change: role="alert" on the delete-error banner; role="status" on the ReportGenerator result line and the Dashboard loading text.
fixed.tests: CJU-02 asserts the delete banner is a role=alert live region, CJU-06 asserts the report status region is a role=status live region carrying the error tone on a failed generate, and the CJU-03 block asserts the dashboard loading state is announced while its fetch is still in flight.

fixed.issue: The facility quota was a count-then-insert across two statements with no row lock, while the CSV quota deliberately used SELECT ... FOR UPDATE. Five parallel POST /api/companies/:id/facilities all read existing.length === 0 and all inserted, putting five facilities on a starter plan whose limit is one.
fixed.change: The cap check and the insert now run in one transaction that takes SELECT id FROM public.companies WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE, mirroring reserveCsvImportQuota. Rejection rolls back instead of leaving the transaction open, and the no-pool sample path keeps the original shape.
fixed.tests: tests/audit-20261005-server.test.ts pins the lock, the ordering of lock/count/insert/commit, and the rollback. Not exercised against a live database here: that requires the Docker-backed suites, which cannot start on this machine, so the concurrency behaviour itself is argued from the transaction shape rather than observed.

fixed.issue: The public sample report — the product's primary proof artifact — contradicted the factor registry. It cited ipcc-ar6-gwp100, an id the registry had already removed, on an AR6 basis, while the calculator standardised on ipcc-ar5-gwp100 because EPA EFH 2025 and eGRID2023 both use AR5 GWPs. Every row carried a fabricated checksum (sha256:ab12, cd34, ef56, gh78, ij90 — four hex digits where SHA-256 is 64). It listed uk-defra-2024 as active when DEFRA is absent from the codebase, and exiobase-3-eeio-2021 as active with the 2022/2021 dates the registry comments describe as fabricated, when EXIOBASE is roadmap-only.
fixed.impact: The core claim is 'every number traces back to a source'. A prospect or auditor downloading the register and checking the checksums would find they verify as nothing and that the GWP basis disagrees with the methodology page.
fixed.change: Register reconciled to registry.ts: AR5 id and basis throughout, eGRID2023 publication year corrected, fabricated checksums cleared, DEFRA row removed, EXIOBASE renamed to exiobase-3.8 with roadmap-not-wired status, and three activity rows' decorated source ('epa-egrid-2023 (CAMX subregion)') normalised so it resolves again. survey-proxy-2026 registered as an explicit internal estimate.
fixed.tests: tests/sample-report-provenance.test.ts — 7 cases covering id resolution, AR5 consistency, roadmap sources never marked active, checksum shape, and fixture/CSV agreement.

fixed.issue: report-generator.cjs validated the register with a hardcoded length of 5, so the count was an accident rather than an invariant and the validator could not detect an incomplete register.
fixed.change: Replaced the count with referential integrity: every factor cited by an activity row must appear in the register. That immediately caught a real gap — the employee-commute proxy was cited by two rows and had never been registered, which the count-based check could not have found.
fixed.tests: tests/sample-report-provenance.test.ts plus the existing audit-regressions suite.

fixed.issue: The chat header read 'EcoAuditor Sales / Online now', implying a staffed live-chat queue. /api/chat is a rule-based state machine — string matches and regex over a fixed script, with no LLM call and no human in the loop.
fixed.change: Now 'EcoAuditor Assistant' / 'Automated · replies instantly'.

fixed.issue: Security.tsx and PrivacyPolicy.tsx described QuickBooks/Xero/OAuth integrations in the present tense, including a read-only data-protection assurance. No such integration exists anywhere in the codebase; pricing.ts, mockData.ts, LandingPage.tsx and llms.txt all mark them roadmap.
fixed.change: Both now state the integrations are roadmap and not available today, keeping the read-only/OAuth commitment scoped to when they ship. A security page should not carry data-handling assurances about systems that do not exist.

fixed.issue: Every /blog/:slug URL fell through to the SPA fallback and served static/index.html. Verified live 2026-10-05: all seven published posts returned the homepage's title, meta description, OG tags and FAQPage JSON-LD, plus <link rel="canonical" href="https://ecoauditor.io/" />.
fixed.impact: A canonical aimed at the homepage explicitly instructs Google to consolidate the post URL away. Combined with a sitemap listing zero post URLs and a prerendered /blog/ containing zero post links, Google had three independent signals to drop every article. Seven high-intent pages (SB 253, CBAM, Scope 3, ESG software selection) were being actively de-indexed.
fixed.change: Added a /blog/:slug route that rewrites the served head per post: own title, description, self-referencing canonical, og:type=article, OG/Twitter tags, and a BlogPosting JSON-LD node in place of the homepage FAQPage. Slugs are shape-checked before the query and failures fall through to existing SPA behaviour. The app still renders the body after hydration; only the head changes.
fixed.tests: tests/blog-post-seo.test.ts (12 cases, including a hostile-title injection attempt) and tests/blog-head-real-shell.test.ts (6 cases running the rewrite against the actual built static/index.html, skipped when no build is present).

fixed.issue: public/sitemap.xml is a static file listing 11 marketing URLs and no blog posts. Posts live in the database and are published without a rebuild, so post URLs could never appear.
fixed.change: Added a dynamic /sitemap.xml that appends published post URLs from blog_posts (lastmod from published_at). Degrades to the marketing page list if the table is missing, and never advertises auth-only /app/* or /auth/* routes. Registered BEFORE express.static — see SEO-03.
fixed.tests: tests/blog-post-seo.test.ts pins the query, the auth-route exclusion, the content type and the fallback.

fixed.issue: Introduced by this run's own SEO-01 change and caught by the escaping test before release: JSON.stringify does not escape <, > or /. A post title containing '</script>' terminates the JSON-LD block early, so the remainder parses as live markup in the served head of every request for that post.
fixed.change: JSON-LD is emitted with <, > and & escaped as JSON unicode sequences, keeping the payload valid JSON while inert as HTML.
fixed.tests: tests/blog-post-seo.test.ts and tests/blog-head-real-shell.test.ts both assert a hostile title cannot break out, and that the block still parses as JSON with the original value intact.

fixed.issue: parseEmissionCsv threw on the first row whose amount was blank or non-numeric, so a 500-row upload with one typo imported nothing at all. It also contradicted the ingest route, which already isolates bad scope, bad confidence and unknown facilities per row and skips only those rows — a blank amount was the single problem that voided an entire customer import.
fixed.impact: The customer fixed line 12, resubmitted, discovered line 47, and repeated. For a paid plan whose differentiator is bulk CSV import of real utility and fuel data, this was the most likely day-one workflow blocker.
fixed.change: Added parseEmissionCsvDetailed returning { rows, errors } and skipping only unparseable rows. Each surviving row carries _rowNumber, because dropped rows mean the array index is no longer the file line and every later diagnostic would name the wrong row of the upload. File-level problems still throw, since a missing column or unterminated quoted field makes the whole file unreadable; parseEmissionCsv is kept as a strict all-or-nothing wrapper so existing callers and boundary tests are unchanged. total_rows now counts parser-rejected rows, so the UI reports '498 of 500 rows imported' against the file the customer actually uploaded.
fixed.tests: tests/csv-partial-import.test.ts — 7 cases covering partial success, exact line numbers, multiple bad rows, the blank-amount-zero guard, file-level throws, the strict wrapper, and a header-only file.

fixed.issue: GET /api/account/export returned only company, facilities and emissionEntries. The `reports` table — which holds title, type, status, last_updated, completeness and signoff — and `csv_import_events` were absent.
fixed.impact: /api/account/delete-data deliberately PRESERVES both tables as the audit trail, so the platform retained data the customer could never obtain a copy of, and could not exercise a data-portability right over it. reports.signoff is the compliance artifact the product exists to produce. The Privacy Policy section 9 tells customers they can export their workspace data at any time, and the claims register approves `no-proprietary-formats` partly on the evidence of that export.
fixed.change: Both audit-trail reads added to the payload. Tenant-scoped, and each degrades to an empty list when its table is missing so an unmigrated database cannot turn a portability request into a 500. The emission-entry cap remains disclosed in notes rather than silently truncating.
fixed.tests: tests/account-export-rights.test.ts — 7 cases including that every public.reports / public.csv_import_events read in the file is tenant-scoped.

fixed.issue: Introduced by SEO-02 and caught only at runtime: the dynamic /sitemap.xml was registered AFTER express.static, which serves static/sitemap.xml (a build-time mirror of public/sitemap.xml). Express matches in registration order, so the static file answered first and the dynamic route never ran.
fixed.impact: The route would have shipped completely inert, so production would still have listed zero blog post URLs — the entire reason it exists. No source-level test could see it, because registration order is invisible to text assertions.
fixed.change: Route moved above express.static; the duplicate further down removed. express.static still mounted, and the blog head route stays below it since it reads static/index.html itself and rewrites the head.
fixed.verification: Found by booting the server locally and diffing the response: the served body carried the static file's lastmod values and its em-dash comment. After the move the response carries the dynamic markers, /pricing still serves from express.static, and /blog/:slug with no database falls through to the SPA rather than erroring.
fixed.tests: tests/route-ordering.test.ts compares indexOf positions directly, asserts the route is registered exactly once, and pins that express.static is still mounted.

fixed.issue: public/robots.txt had `User-agent: *` carrying nothing but `Allow: /`. The auth-only disallows sat at the bottom of the file, after the Applebot-Extended block. In robots.txt, directives after a `User-agent:` line belong to that group and the group ends at the next `User-agent:` line, so those disallows attached to Applebot alone.
fixed.impact: Verified against the live file on 2026-10-05: Googlebot matches the wildcard group and was therefore explicitly permitted to crawl /app/, /auth/, /login, /signup and /forgot-password — exactly the surfaces the file claimed to protect. A naive substring check would have passed, since the paths are present in the text.
fixed.change: The auth-only disallows moved inside the wildcard group; the named AI agents keep their own groups, which are allowed to differ from the wildcard. Sitemap declaration moved to the end where it belongs.
fixed.tests: tests/robots-txt.test.ts parses the file the way a crawler does (RFC 9309 group semantics) instead of substring-matching, and embeds the previous wildcard group as a fixture so the test cannot pass vacuously.

fixed.issue: APP_BASE_URL falls back to http://localhost:3000 when APP_URL is unset. The hard boot-time throw that guards it was coupled to STRIPE_SECRET_KEY — deliberately, because an unconditional throw would crash-loop any production-mode preview deploy that has no Stripe key. That coupling was sound while APP_BASE_URL fed only Stripe redirects. SEO-03 then made it feed /sitemap.xml and the /blog/:slug canonical, so a production deploy without billing (a preview box, or a deploy taken while Stripe is being rotated out) passed the guard and served localhost URLs.
fixed.impact: Latent, not live: production currently sets APP_URL, and the Stripe-coupled throw keeps it set, so the shipped sitemap is correct. The exposure is the silent-failure shape — the server boots clean, logs nothing, and every <loc> in the sitemap reads <loc>http://localhost:3000/…</loc>. Crawlers get an unreachable origin, search visibility collapses over weeks, and nothing in the logs connects it to a missing env var. Found by the new runtime smoke gate, which booted the server with no APP_URL: the static mirror had the right origin, so every source-level test reading public/ saw a healthy file.
fixed.change: startServer() now logs at error level whenever NODE_ENV=production and APP_URL is unset, independent of Stripe, naming the two affected surfaces. checks: Route sweep over 20 paths including unknown pages and /app/*: no 500s. The 301s on bare marketing paths are express.static directory redirects, one hop before a 200.

Adversarial blog slugs (' OR 1=1--, ../../etc/passwd, %00, newline injection, <script>, a/b/c, UPPER-Case) all fall through to the SPA with no crash and no injection.

Unauthenticated requests to every data-bearing endpoint are refused; none returns 2xx. apiAuthGuard returns 503 when the auth backend is unconfigured, dev auth requires ALLOW_DEV_AUTH plus an exact DEV_AUTH_SECRET match, and req.user is assigned only after a validated session.

Security headers ship live including Strict-Transport-Security with preload. Rate limiting is applied to all /api/ paths with the Stripe webhook exempt for a documented reason, and resolveClientIp validates Cloudflare X-Forwarded-For against the published egress ranges.
Password reset avoids being an account-existence oracle (404 deliberately swallowed) and handles the 'I already have a code' path without an email in state.
Plan gates are genuinely enforced: the CSV import quota counts from public.csv_import_events under a row lock, and Scope 3 is gated on both /api/calculate and /api/ingest/csv.

resolved_without_change.conclusion: Not fixable as reported, and not a production exposure. The advisory GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm affects braces <=3.0.3 and 3.0.3 is the highest version ever published, so every available release is affected and there is no patched version to move to. It reaches the tree only through tailwindcss@3.4.19 (chokidar 3.6.0, micromatch 4.0.8), and `npm ls braces --omit=dev` is empty — it is absent from the production dependency tree entirely. npm's only suggested fix is tailwindcss 4.x, which AGENTS.md explicitly forbids. Closing this requires either an upstream braces release or relaxing the Tailwind constraint; it is not a code defect.

The three Docker-backed suites (32 tests) cannot start on this machine because Docker is absent; they are not skipped in CI. .github/workflows/security.yml runs `npm run build && npm test` on ubuntu-latest, which ships Docker, so they execute there. This is a local environment limitation, not a repository defect.

Still not derivable. open.issue: The CSRD scope thresholds may be superseded again. Multiple secondary sources (EY, BDO, Taylor Wessing, Deloitte) report that a Content Directive entered into force on 18 March 2026 raising mandatory CSRD scope to more than 1,000 employees AND more than EUR450m turnover, with transposition due 19 March 2027, removing wave 3 and allowing Member States to exempt wave 1 companies below the revised thresholds for FY2025 and FY2026.
open.why_open: Deliberately NOT encoded in compliance-deadlines.cjs. Transposition is national and Member States have exemption options, so the operative scope for any given Member State cannot be resolved from the Directive text alone, and no public surface states a CSRD date that would now be wrong. Encoding a half-verified threshold change into a compliance verdict would trade a known-stale date for a new, less-well-grounded one. The primary text was not verified on EUR-Lex during this run, unlike COMP-03 where it was.
open.required: Confirm the instrument and its number on EUR-Lex, then decide with the customer which Member State(s) are supported. Until then the wave 1 (>500 employees) and wave 2 (>250 employees) criteria stand as the last verified state. Note the product currently cannot answer this question for a real tenant anyway, since company revenue/employees/region are not modelled and /api/companies/:id/compliance answers 501.
